name: Actuarial Science
boundaries: Actuarial Science: fundamental discoveries and enabling technologies within this field. Include cross-field consequences where the central advance belongs to this field; exclude routine incremental optimization. Use the historical breakthroughs in the prompt to calibrate revolutionary impact.

original_dispositions.reason: The entry removes the claim that all future medical and social shocks can be forecast precisely or that forecasting alone ends reserve errors.

Causal analysis can reveal mechanisms and trade-offs, but a universal guarantee of fairness and regulatory approval is not a scientific consequence of identifying causal factors. Olivier Côté, Marie-Pier Côté and Arthur Charpentier present different families of fair scores rather than a single universally privileged definition; they describe “a spectrum of fair score families” in “A fair price to pay: Exploiting causal graphs for fairness in insurance,” 2025, §§7–8, DOI: 10.1111/jori.12503: https://onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/10.1111/jori.12503

original_dispositions.original_title: Coherent, elicitable and backtestable multi-period risk measure
original_dispositions.reason: Such mathematical properties are useful, but the proposed “single number” would not itself supply reliable long-horizon loss distributions or resolve capital and social choices. Existing theory also requires care about which properties hold: expected shortfall is not individually elicitable in the cited setting, while the pair of value-at-risk and expected shortfall is jointly elicitable. Source: “Elicitability and identifiability of set-valued measures of systemic risk,” 2021, introduction, DOI: 10.1007/s00780-020-00446-z: https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007/s00780-020-00446-z
Perfect prediction replaced by separately testable pricing consistency, real-world calibration and model uncertainty.

original_dispositions.original_title: Forward-looking climate and catastrophe pricing and reserving
original_dispositions.reason: Covered by ACT-01 for physical catastrophe-loss distributions and ACT-03 for financing the resulting correlated losses. Transition-risk modeling is not fully covered; no distinct actuarial breakthrough for it was established in this pass.

original_dispositions.original_title: Stable healthcare cost and utilization model
original_dispositions.reason: Limited to evidence-supported, conditional projections rather than a universal model or a solution to healthcare funding.

original_dispositions.original_title: Provably fair and explainable machine learning for all actuarial uses
original_dispositions.reason: Explainability, robustness and particular fairness properties are valuable, but a guarantee satisfying every definition and application is not established, and normative trade-offs remain. The Côté and colleagues source under item 2 illustrates the issue.

Covered in part by ACT-03’s practical financing architecture. A universal real-time social optimum is not added: the objectives, information, institutions and allocation of losses are contested, and an optimum would not itself provide loss-absorbing capital.

Better causal and behavioral models could improve particular products, but the research reviewed here did not establish a distinct capability at the requested revolutionary threshold. Adverse selection, moral hazard and lapse behavior also involve different mechanisms; a universal solution cannot be assumed.

The historical promise of adequate lifetime benefits under every combination of investment, demographic and longevity outcomes, without benefit adjustment or outside resources, is not supported. ACT-07 instead proposes accessible pooling with explicit loss allocation.
